stories.primary_headline: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack

primary_source.headline: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
primary_source.content: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, close to Ukrainian cargo planes, on 4 August. It failed to explode as the detonator was apparently faulty, and investigators suspect a second drone collided with a cargo aircraft nearby. A third drone was reportedly found near the airport 10 days later. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the Leipzig airport attack followed the "well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe" and the assumption was that Germany would be targeted again. Security experts had speculated that Russia may have been responsible, however Russia has always rejected claims of involvement. Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carries most of the country's aerial cargo. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, who was standing beside Dobrindt at a press conference in Berlin, said he would order the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, and the contract for the Russian House in Berlin will also be terminated - which many observers have said has been used for espionage and to spread Russian propaganda.

sources.headline: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
Germany blames Russia for drone attack on Leipzig airport - CNN

stories.brief: On August 4, a drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport, a critical hub for German military, NATO allies, and Ukraine's Antonov Airlines, with a second drone suspected of colliding with an aircraft and a third found later, prompting initial suspicions of Russian involvement despite Moscow's denials. German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt has now officially attributed the incident to Russia, characterizing it as consistent with 'well-established patterns of Russian hybrid operations in Europe.' In a direct response, Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn and the termination of the contract for the Russian House in Berlin, which has long been suspected of facilitating espionage and propaganda.

why_it_matters_bullets: This decisive action marks a significant escalation in Germany's stance against suspected Russian aggression, signaling a proactive defense against future hybrid attacks and deepening the diplomatic rift, with Dobrindt anticipating further targeting of Germany.

stories.primary_headline: Govt hikes windfall gains tax on petrol, diesel exports; cuts levy on ATF

primary_source.headline: Govt hikes windfall gains tax on petrol, diesel exports; cuts levy on ATF
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The government on Tuesday hiked windfall gains tax on export of petrol and diesel, and reduced it marginally on ATF for the next fortnight.The rate of special additional excise duty (SAED) along with road and infrastructure cess on export of diesel now stands at Rs 25 per litre, up from Rs 24 a litre. SAED on export of aviation turbine fuel (ATF) has been set at Rs 19 per litre, compared to Rs 19.5 per litre earlier.E20 in the sky? Definitely not, says Civil Aviation Minister Naidu, denies rumours of ethanol blend with ATFThe duty on petrol exports has been hiked to Rs 1.5 per litre effective September 1, up from zero earlier.The Finance Ministry in a notification said the duty hikes will be effective from September 1.Amid escalating tensions in West Asia, the Government imposed an export duty on diesel and ATF on March 27 and revised the rate every fortnight.  Beginning May 16,  the levy was imposed on petrol exports.The ministry also said that there is no change in the existing duty rates on petrol and diesel cleared for domestic consumption.Airlines shun Rs 10,000-crore ATF subsidy as fuel prices fallThe windfall tax was levied to increase domestic availability of the fuel amid the war in West Asia.It was also aimed at preventing exporters from taking undue advantage due to price differences as global crude oil prices had increased since the war began.The windfall tax was intended to ensure domestic availability of petroleum products by disincentivising exports amid the West Asia crisis.

stories.primary_headline: CM Vijay can even become US President, says AIADMK chief Palaniswami

primary_source.headline: CM Vijay can even become US President, says AIADMK chief Palaniswami
primary_source.content: Coimbatore (TN): Mocking the ruling TVK's extensive public relations campaigns and Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's penchant for chartered flights, AIADMK General Secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami on Tuesday sarcastically remarked that the TN CM could even go on to become the President of the United States.Responding to a reporter's query about TVK supporters projecting CM Vijay as a future Prime Minister, Palaniswami deployed heavy sarcasm.Tamil Nadu CM Vijay releases water from Mettur Dam"He could even become the President of America. There is nothing wrong with it, it is his wish," former Chief Minister remarked.However, dismissing the state government's reliance on social media optics, he said, "They are running the government by putting out 'reels' here; that won't work there." He also branded CM Vijay a “costly Chief Minister,” and contrasted the current administration's expenditure with that of former Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa."During Amma's tenure, projects were inaugurated via video conferencing to cut costs," Palaniswami said, mocking the irony of Vijay projecting a humble farmer image while indulging in such expensive travel.Shifting focus to the state's administrative machinery, Palaniswami alleged a complete breakdown in governance.Pointing out that Coimbatore alone had witnessed nearly nine murders in a single month, he stated, "Within 110 days, the law and order situation has completely collapsed. Wherever you look, murders, robberies, and clashes are increasing".The AIADMK leader further accused the Chief Minister of "recklessly announcing schemes" under Rule 110 without fiscal backing.Tamil Nadu CM Vijay announces further hike in milk procurement prices, unveils multi-crore infra pushHe warned that if the state continued borrowing at the current rate, its debt could balloon to Rs 10 lakh crore.Highlighting the steep rise in the prices of essential commodities, including rice, sugar, and cooking oil, he said the government had taken no tangible steps to control inflation.Citing rising corruption and widespread protests by farmers, nurses, and the general public, Palaniswami confidently predicted an early end to the DMK’s tenure. "Looking at all this, this government will not last for five years," he added.

primary_source.headline: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari lunches 'Arjun Vahini' for early-stage disaster response
primary_source.content: Kolkata: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday launched 'Arjun Vahini' for early-stage disaster response, initially comprising 200 personnel, primarily retired soldiers and former Agniveers.Of the 200 personnel, 100 will be deployed in Kolkata, while 50 each will be stationed in the hills and the Sundarbans, he told reporters at the state secretariat."The force will be tasked with responding to disasters and emergencies," the chief minister said.The Sunday Story | The first Agniveers are about to leave. stories.primary_headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay releases water from Mettur Dam

primary_source.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay releases water from Mettur Dam
primary_source.content: Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Tuesday threw open the sluices of the Stanley Reservoir in Mettur, releasing water for irrigation in the fertile Cauvery Delta region after the dam’s water level touched 90 feet. The dam was not opened on its designated date of June 12 due to the non-availability of water, as Karnataka failed to adhere to the monthly schedule of water release stipulated by the Supreme Court.Dressed in a silk shirt and silk veshti, Vijay worshipped the water before showering it with flowers as a mark of releasing water from the dam, which is the lifeline of lakhs of farmers in the Cauvery Delta region comprising Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, and Mayiladuthurai districts.Tuesday was chosen for the dam’s opening since the water level reached 90 feet last week — following the established practice that water is released only when the level touches 90 feet to ensure sustained supplies over months. The water level at the dam stood at 91.56 feet, storage at 54.452 tmcft, and the inflow at 10,857 cusecs.Explainer | The Mettur dam and why water released from the reservoir is the lifeline for lakhs of farmers in Cauvery Delta regionThe discharge was increased to 5,000 cusecs at 4:00 PM from 3,000 cusecs at 11:00 AM, and further increased to 7,000 cusecs at 8:00 PM on Tuesday.“Water is being released through the dam powerhouse and tunnel powerhouse. The barrages have been informed to maintain the discharge without any deviation,” a senior government official told&nbsp;DH.Vijay drove from the Salem Airport to&nbsp;Mettur — a&nbsp;distance of 51 kilometers — with people lining both sides of the road to give him a rousing reception. After the event, Vijay visited a farmer's home, met residents near Mettur, interacted with them, gifted a saree to the farmer's wife, and posed for pictures with elderly women.While water from the dam is generally released for the cultivation of&nbsp;kuruvai&nbsp;(short-term crop) on June 12, the schedule could not be maintained this year.&nbsp;Kuruvai&nbsp;has effectively failed in the Delta region, with farmers claiming that paddy was cultivated on only about 2 lakh acres, down from last year’s record cultivation of 6.30 lakh acres.Samba&nbsp;is generally cultivated across an area of about 10.5 lakh to 11 lakh acres in the four districts.The water released from the Mettur Dam will be used for the&nbsp;samba&nbsp;(long-term crop) this year, with farmer associations urging cultivators to adopt direct-sowing methods to save time. The government plans to release about 1 tmcft of water a day for 45 days, relying on the onset of the Northeast Monsoon (NEM) in mid-October to sustain the crop.“Since we need water for the whole season, we are asking our people to sow the seeds directly instead of using the regular cultivation method. We need to conserve water and use the available water judiciously,” P.R. Pandian, general secretary of the Tamil Nadu Cauvery Farmers’ Association, told&nbsp;DH.

stories.primary_headline: Iran attacks Jordan, UAE after US bombs Larak Island: what's the latest?

primary_source.headline: Iran attacks Jordan, UAE after US bombs Larak Island: What’s the latest? - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Iran says it has attacked US bases in Jordan and US military assets in the United Arab Emirates in retaliation for strikes on Larak Island in the first active exchange between the two sides since late July. The Iranian response came after the United States claimed to have hit two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. A US official told Al Jazeera Arabic following the attack that the launchers were preparing to fire missiles carrying naval mines towards the waterway. In his first comments since the attack, President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was “not looking for war”, but would “never sit still in the face of any aggression” either. Iran “will give a decisive response to the aggressors” if attacked, Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by the Iranian news agency Fars. “Instability and unrest in the region are not in the interest of any country and will challenge everyone.” Here’s what we know so far and what could happen to the diplomatic efforts to end the six-month-old war that has disrupted global oil supply and jolted the global economy. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said the US attacks on Sunday night had killed and wounded several Iranian soldiers and civilians.
